messages:
emma: Heads-up — onboarding run for mosaic-7b-lite failed during Redwood conversion. Looks like several shard tensors came through with an unexpected key prefix (e.g. 'module/encoder.wte' -> 'hf_prefix/module/encoder.wte') and kv-cache step explodes after quant.
raj: Ugh, prefix bleed. Is that coming from the HF hub snapshot or our converter mapping? Any stack trace?
nate: I pulled the build logs, converter raised KeyError in weight_map.apply:
```
KeyError: 'encoder.wte' not found
at converter/loader.py:142
```
convert-bot: CI job 4821 finished: converter-smoke (mosaic-7b-lite) — FAIL
emma: I downloaded the raw shards from hub and inspected the keys with `safetensors info` — the keys include `revision_meta.source` and a weird `author_prefix` field. Not all shards have it, only the last two (shard_07, shard_08).
raj: That smells like a partial upstream transform on those files. Maybe whoever uploaded did an intermediate checkpoint with a wrapper. Can you paste one key listing?
emma: Sure:
```
shard_07.safetensors:
  hf_prefix/module/encoder.wte
  hf_prefix/module/encoder.layer.0.attn.q.weight
  hf_prefix/module/decoder.wte
```
nate: Our converter expects raw weight names and strips known prefixes (`model.` `module.`). It doesn't handle arbitrary `hf_prefix/`.
emma: Repro steps: convert with `rw-convert --model-dir ./mosaic-7b-lite --out ./rw` -> conversion completes but runtime load mismatch at inference when kvcache lookup fails.
raj: Quick fix idea: add a normalizer pass that strips any leading token that matches `/^[a-z0-9_]+\//` up to a max length and then run existing rename rules. But we should be careful — some prefixes might be semantically important.
convert-bot: New PR opened: redwood/convert#708 — attempt/key-normalizer. Tests: unit on name normalization added.
nate: Will run local quantization with that branch. If normalization maps two different keys to same canonical name we must detect collisions and abort.
emma: Also noticed hub download for that model uses an auth-scoped CDN URL. Our downloader retried once then fell back to partial file, which could explain why only later shards had the weird metadata (maybe uploaded mid-way). Logging from downloader:
```
WARN: hub-fetch: 403 transient, retrying (1/3)
INFO: download shard_07.safetensors -> partial-temp-abc
ERROR: shard checksum mismatch for shard_08
```
raj: Add checksum-and-meta verification after download before conversion. If metadata differs from expectations, fail fast and surface to uploader.
nate: Ran quick smoke with PR branch — converter normalizes `hf_prefix/` and conversion finishes. But two weight names collided (they had `hf_prefix/module/encoder.wte` and `module/encoder.wte`) — the PR flags collision and aborts with a clear message.
emma: Looks good. We should also add a post-convert validation: load model, run a short forward with dummy tokens and check kv-cache read/write consistency.
convert-bot: CI job 4829 started: convert-integration (PR 708)
ci-bot: CI job 4829 passed: convert-integration (PR 708) :white_check_mark:
raj: Next: patch the downloader for stronger retries and ensure we always download to a unique temp path (avoid partial reuse). Also add a warning in onboarding doc about vendor artifacts and prefix wrappers.
emma: I'll follow up with support to ask uploader to republish a clean snapshot and also run a quick eval baseline (perplexity on dev set) to ensure no silent regressions after normalization.
nate: I'll queue a canary rollout for mosaic-7b-lite on dedicated infra after deploy, with the new hash and the KV-check smoke enabled.
emma: Thanks all. Leaving the PR to the eng-ml oncall to merge after canary results.
